newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS SEEN DOWN, AWAITING IMF LOAN TALKS.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS SEEN DOWN, AWAITING IMF LOAN TALKS.

text.p: The Thai bourse was expected to decline slightly on Friday as investors did not want to hold stocks over the weekend while they also waited for IMF talks about loans for Thailand next week, brokers said.

"I think the market will rise marginally at the open but will start to decline later in the day. Investors aren't willing to hold stocks over the weekend. They're also waiting for talks on IMF loans to Thailand," said Danai Tunyathisitchai of Dhana Siam Finance.
The composite SET index closed 2.72 points higher at 638.04 on 5.9 billion baht turnover on Thursday.

The IMF said lender states and international financial institutions will meet in Tokyo on Monday to discuss the multi-billion dollar package, designed to help Thailand recover from its economic crisis.

Thai finance ministry sources said on Thursday that Thailand was likely to seek $7 billion from Japan, $4 billion from the IMF, $1 billion from the World Bank and $1 billion from the Asian Development Bank.
